title: A flashing check engine light is not the same warning as a steady one
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: Check engine light flashing, or steady?
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up dashboard instrument cluster at night, check engine light icon blinking on/off in a dark cabin, shallow depth of field, subtle camera drift in.

beats.narration: Those are not the same warning.
beats.visualPrompt: Same dashboard, check engine light now steady/solid (no blink), slow push-in, contrast lighting to visually separate from beat 1.

beats.narration: Flashing usually points to a misfire dumping raw fuel into a red-hot catalytic converter.
beats.visualPrompt: Engine bay, close macro shot of exhaust manifold glowing faint heat-shimmer, slow pan across metal surface, practical orange/red rim light.

beats.narration: Keep driving on it and that converter can cook.
beats.visualPrompt: Catalytic converter cutaway or exhaust underbody shot, camera tilts up from tailpipe along the exhaust line, muted industrial color grade.

beats.narration: So ease off the gas and skip the highway.
beats.visualPrompt: Speedometer needle easing down from higher speed to lower speed, close macro, subtle motion blur on the needle only.

beats.narration: Steady is different: worth checking soon.
beats.visualPrompt: Wide shop bay establishing shot, vehicle on a lift or parked in a bay, calm even lighting, static-to-slow-dolly.
Nick's Tire & Auto branded shop-front or bay signage plate (existing brand asset, do not generate new logo), gentle push-in, held final frame for 3s SAVE freeze.
